newsitem.title: USA: Airport Systems end-FY97 backlog rises.
newsitem.headline: Airport Systems end-FY97 backlog rises.

text.p: Airport Systems International Inc, which makes ground-based equipment and airfield signage for airports, said Thursday it ended fiscal 1997 with a backlog of $19.3 million, up from $6.5 million a year ago.

"That improvement suggests a continuation of the company's positive financial performance into fiscal 1998," Keith Cowan, president, said in a statement. "The underlying need remains strong to upgrade and expand airports, and their related navaid (navigational aid) equipment and systems, on a global basis."
He added that the company's financial position remains strong with $3.1 million in cash and short-term investments and virtually no short-term debt at the close of fiscal 1997.
"We are optimistic that our strong balance sheet will help the company to extend the sound momentum that was established during fiscal 1997," Cowan said.

Earlier, Airport Systems reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended April 30 of $0.21 a share, up from $0.10 a year ago. For fiscal 1997, it earned $0.25 a share, compared with a net loss of $0.10.
